sanskrit: śrotavyaṃ hitakāmānāṃ suhṛdāṃ bhūtim icchatām na kartavyo hi nirbandho nirbandho hi kṣayodayaḥ
english: Those who wish well-being for their friends and desire their prosperity should listen: one must not persist stubbornly, for stubborn insistence is the seed of ruin.

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api gāndhāre mānaṃ krodhaṃ ca varjaya saṃdhatsva pāṇḍavair vīra saṃrambhaṃ tyaja pārthiva
english: Therefore you too, O son of Gāndhārī, abandon pride and anger; make peace with the Pāṇḍavas, O hero; relinquish your fury, O king.

sanskrit: dadāti yat pārthiva yat karoti; yad vā tapas tapyati yaj juhoti na tasya nāśo 'sti na cāpakarṣo; nānyas tad aśnāti sa eva kartā
english: Whatever a king gives, whatever he does, whatever austerity he practises, whatever oblation he offers — none of it is lost or diminished; no other reaps it: the doer alone enjoys the fruit.

sanskrit: idaṃ mahākhyānam anuttamaṃ mataṃ; bahuśrutānāṃ gataroṣarāgiṇām samīkṣya loke bahudhā pradhāvitā; trivargadṛṣṭiḥ pṛthivīm upāśnute
english: This great narrative is held to be unsurpassed by the learned who are free from passion and anger; having considered it, the one who pursues the three ends of life in their right order enjoys the earth in its entirety.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhagavann evam evaitad yathā vadasi nārada icchāmi cāham apy evaṃ na tv īśo bhagavann aham
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Revered sage, it is exactly as you say; I too desire this very thing, yet I am not master of it, O blessed one.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tataḥ kṛṣṇam abhyabhāṣata bhārata svargyaṃ lokyaṃ ca mām āttha dharmyaṃ nyāyyaṃ ca keśava
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, he then addressed Kṛṣṇa, O Bhārata: "You have told me what leads to heaven and to worldly good, what is righteous and just, O Keśava."

sanskrit: na tv ahaṃ svavaśas tāta kriyamāṇaṃ na me priyam aṅga duryodhanaṃ kṛṣṇa mandaṃ śāstrātigaṃ mama
english: "But I am not my own master, dear one; what is being done is not pleasing to me — Duryodhana, O Kṛṣṇa, is dull-witted and transgresses the scripture, yet he is my son."

sanskrit: anunetuṃ mahābāho yatasva puruṣottama suhṛtkāryaṃ tu sumahat kṛtaṃ te syāj janārdana
english: "Strive to appease him, O mighty-armed one, O best of men; you would thereby perform a very great service to your friends, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: tato 'bhyāvṛtya vārṣṇeyo duryodhanam amarṣaṇam abravīn madhurāṃ vācaṃ sarvadharmārthatattvavit
english: Then the Vṛṣṇi hero, knowing the truth of all dharma and worldly good, turned and spoke gentle words to the impatient Duryodhana.

sanskrit: duryodhana nibodhedaṃ madvākyaṃ kurusattama samarthaṃ te viśeṣeṇa sānubandhasya bhārata
english: "Hear this my word, O best of the Kurus; it is especially beneficial to you and to those bound to you, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: mahāprājña kule jātaḥ sādhv etat kartum arhasi śrutavṛttopasaṃpannaḥ sarvaiḥ samudito guṇaiḥ
english: "O greatly wise one, born of a noble lineage, endowed with learning and right conduct, praised for all your qualities — it is fitting that you do what is good."

sanskrit: dauṣkuleyā durātmāno nṛśaṃsā nirapatrapāḥ ta etad īdṛśaṃ kuryur yathā tvaṃ tāta manyase
english: "Those of bad family, evil-minded, cruel, and shameless — they would act in the way you are now contemplating, dear boy."

sanskrit: dharmārthayuktā loke 'smin pravṛttir lakṣyate satām asatāṃ viparītā tu lakṣyate bharatarṣabha
english: "In this world, the conduct of the righteous is seen to be joined with dharma and worldly good; the conduct of the wicked is seen to be the reverse, O bull among Bhāratas."

sanskrit: viparītā tv iyaṃ vṛttir asakṛl lakṣyate tvayi adharmaś cānubandho 'tra ghoraḥ prāṇaharo mahān
english: "This reverse conduct is again and again observed in you; the unrighteousness bound up with it is dreadful and great — it destroys one's very life."

sanskrit: anekaśas tvannimittam ayaśasyaṃ ca bhārata tam anarthaṃ pariharann ātmaśreyaḥ kariṣyasi
english: "Because of you, infamy has arisen many times, O Bhārata; by avoiding that harmful course of action you will act for your own welfare."

sanskrit: bhrātṝṇām atha bhṛtyānāṃ mitrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa adharmyād ayaśasyāc ca karmaṇas tvaṃ pramokṣyase
english: "You will thereby free yourself, your brothers, your servants, and your friends from unrighteous and infamous action, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: prājñaiḥ śūrair mahotsāhair ātmavadbhir bahuśrutaiḥ saṃdhatsva puruṣavyāghra pāṇḍavair bharatarṣabha
english: "Make peace with the Pāṇḍavas — wise, brave, highly spirited, self-controlled, and learned men — O tiger among men, O bull among Bhāratas."

sanskrit: tad dhitaṃ ca priyaṃ caiva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya dhīmataḥ pitāmahasya droṇasya vidurasya mahāmateḥ
english: "That would be beneficial and dear to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, to the grandsire, to Droṇa, and to the great-minded Vidura."

sanskrit: kṛpasya somadattasya bāhlīkasya ca dhīmataḥ aśvatthāmno vikarṇasya saṃjayasya viśāṃ pate
english: "And to Kṛpa, to Somadatta, to the wise Bāhlika, to Aśvatthāmā, to Vikarṇa, and to Sañjaya, O lord of the people."

sanskrit: jñātīnāṃ caiva bhūyiṣṭhaṃ mitrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa śame śarma bhavet tāta sarvasya jagatas tathā
english: "And it would bring happiness to the majority of your kinsmen and friends, O scorcher of enemies; in peace there would be welfare for all the world as well, dear boy."

sanskrit: hrīmān asi kule jātaḥ śrutavān anṛśaṃsavān tiṣṭha tāta pituḥ śāstre mātuś ca bharatarṣabha
english: "You are modest, born of a noble house, learned and not cruel; abide, dear boy, within the instruction of your father and your mother, O bull among Bhāratas."

sanskrit: etac chreyo hi manyante pitā yac chāsti bhārata uttamāpadgataḥ sarvaḥ pituḥ smarati śāsanam
english: "Whatever a father commands is held to be the greatest good, O Bhārata; every person in the highest adversity remembers a father's instruction."

sanskrit: rocate te pitus tāta pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃgamaḥ sāmātyasya kuruśreṣṭha tat tubhyaṃ tāta rocatām
english: "Your father together with his ministers desires, dear boy, a meeting with the Pāṇḍavas, O best of Kurus; let that be pleasing to you as well, dear boy."

sanskrit: śrutvā yaḥ suhṛdāṃ śāstraṃ martyo na pratipadyate vipākānte dahaty enaṃ kiṃpākam iva bhakṣitam
english: "The mortal who, having heard the counsel of friends, does not follow it — at the end it burns him, like the kiṃpāka fruit when eaten."

sanskrit: yas tu niḥśreyasaṃ vākyaṃ mohān na pratipadyate sa dīrghasūtro hīnārthaḥ paścāttāpena yujyate
english: "He who, out of delusion, does not accept advice that leads to the highest good — he is dilatory, falls short of his aims, and is yoked to remorse."

sanskrit: yas tu niḥśreyasaṃ śrutvā prāptam evābhipadyate ātmano matam utsṛjya sa loke sukham edhate
english: "But he who, having heard advice leading to the highest good, acts upon what is at hand and sets aside his own wilfulness — he prospers in happiness in this world."

sanskrit: yo 'rthakāmasya vacanaṃ prātikūlyān na mṛṣyate śṛṇoti pratikūlāni dviṣatāṃ vaśam eti saḥ
english: "He who, out of contrariness, will not tolerate the counsel of one who seeks his benefit, hears only things contrary to his good, and falls into the power of his enemies."

sanskrit: satāṃ matam atikramya yo 'satāṃ vartate mate śocante vyasane tasya suhṛdo nacirād iva
english: "He who, transgressing the view of the virtuous, acts according to the view of the wicked — his friends soon grieve for him in his calamity."

sanskrit: mukhyān amātyān utsṛjya yo nihīnān niṣevate sa ghorām āpadaṃ prāpya nottāram adhigacchati
english: "He who abandons his principal ministers and resorts to those of low character, on falling into terrible danger finds no way out."

sanskrit: yo 'satsevī vṛthācāro na śrotā suhṛdāṃ sadā parān vṛṇīte svān dveṣṭi taṃ gauḥ śapati bhārata
english: "He who associates with the wicked, who is idle in conduct, who never listens to friends, who chooses strangers and hates his own — the earth curses him, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ virudhya tair vīrair anyebhyas trāṇam icchasi aśiṣṭebhyo 'samarthebhyo mūḍhebhyo bharatarṣabha
english: "Yet you, having set yourself against those heroes, seek protection from the uncultured, the incompetent, and the foolish, O bull among Bhāratas."

sanskrit: ko hi śakrasamāñ jñātīn atikramya mahārathān anyebhyas trāṇam āśaṃset tvad anyo bhuvi mānavaḥ
english: "What other man on earth, besides you, would pass over kinsmen equal to Indra, great warriors all, and hope for protection from others?"

sanskrit: janmaprabhṛti kaunteyā nityaṃ vinikṛtās tvayā na ca te jātu kupyanti dharmātmāno hi pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "From birth the sons of Kuntī have been constantly wronged by you, yet they never become angry with you — for the Pāṇḍavas are righteous-souled."

sanskrit: mithyāpracaritās tāta janmaprabhṛti pāṇḍavāḥ tvayi samyaṅ mahābāho pratipannā yaśasvinaḥ
english: "The illustrious Pāṇḍavas have been treated with falsehood since birth, dear boy, yet they have responded to you rightly, O mighty-armed one."

sanskrit: tvayāpi pratipattavyaṃ tathaiva bharatarṣabha sveṣu bandhuṣu mukhyeṣu mā manyuvaśam anvagāḥ
english: "You too should respond in kind, O bull among Bhāratas; do not follow the lead of anger toward your own foremost kinsmen."

sanskrit: trivargayuktā prājñānām ārambhā bharatarṣabha dharmārthāv anurudhyante trivargāsaṃbhave narāḥ
english: "The undertakings of the wise are joined with the three ends of life, O bull among Bhāratas; men follow dharma and artha when the three together cannot be achieved."

sanskrit: pṛthak tu viniviṣṭānāṃ dharmaṃ dhīro 'nurudhyate madhyamo 'rthaṃ kaliṃ bālaḥ kāmam evānurudhyate
english: "Among those who pursue them separately: the wise man follows dharma, the middling man follows artha, the quarrelsome man follows kali, and the childish man follows kāma alone."

sanskrit: indriyaiḥ prasṛto lobhād dharmaṃ viprajahāti yaḥ kāmārthāv anupāyena lipsamāno vinaśyati
english: "He who, led by his senses out of greed, abandons dharma, and seeks kāma and artha by improper means — he perishes."

sanskrit: kāmārthau lipsamānas tu dharmam evāditaś caret na hi dharmād apaity arthaḥ kāmo vāpi kadā cana
english: "But he who seeks kāma and artha should follow dharma first of all; for neither artha nor kāma ever departs from dharma."

sanskrit: upāyaṃ dharmam evāhus trivargasya viśāṃ pate lipsamāno hi tenāśu kakṣe 'gnir iva vardhate
english: "Dharma itself is declared to be the means to all three ends, O lord of the people; for one who seeks them through it grows swiftly, like fire in dry grass."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ tātānupāyena lipsase bharatarṣabha ādhirājyaṃ mahad dīptaṃ prathitaṃ sarvarājasu
english: "Yet you, dear boy, are seeking by improper means, O bull among Bhāratas, the great resplendent supremacy renowned among all kings."

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ takṣati hy eṣa vanaṃ paraśunā yathā yaḥ samyag vartamāneṣu mithyā rājan pravartate
english: "He who acts wrongly toward those who act rightly cuts himself down, O king, as an axe cuts a forest."

sanskrit: na tasya hi matiṃ chindyād yasya necchet parābhavam avicchinnasya dhīrasya kalyāṇe dhīyate matiḥ
english: "One should not cut down the mind of one whose defeat one does not desire; the mind of the steadfast whose understanding is unbroken is set upon the good."

sanskrit: tyaktātmānaṃ na bādheta triṣu lokeṣu bhārata apy anyaṃ prākṛtaṃ kiṃ cit kim u tān pāṇḍavarṣabhān
english: "One who has abandoned his own self cannot harm even an ordinary creature in the three worlds, O Bhārata — how much less those bulls among the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: amarṣavaśam āpanno na kiṃ cid budhyate naraḥ chidyate hy ātataṃ sarvaṃ pramāṇaṃ paśya bhārata
english: "A man fallen under the sway of wrath discerns nothing; all extended judgment is cut away — observe this, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: śreyas te durjanāt tāta pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃgamaḥ tair hi saṃprīyamāṇas tvaṃ sarvān kāmān avāpsyasi
english: "Meeting with the Pāṇḍavas is better for you than keeping bad company, dear boy; finding delight in them, you will obtain all your desires."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavair nirjitāṃ bhūmiṃ bhuñjāno rājasattama pāṇḍavān pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā trāṇam āśaṃsase 'nyataḥ
english: "You enjoy the earth won by the Pāṇḍavas, O best of kings, yet placing the Pāṇḍavas behind your back, you seek protection elsewhere."

sanskrit: duḥśāsane durviṣahe karṇe cāpi sasaubale eteṣv aiśvaryam ādhāya bhūtim icchasi bhārata
english: "You place your sovereignty in Duḥśāsana, in the unbearable Karṇa, and in the son of Subala, and through them you seek prosperity, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: na caite tava paryāptā jñāne dharmārthayos tathā vikrame cāpy aparyāptāḥ pāṇḍavān prati bhārata
english: "Yet these are not adequate for you in wisdom, in dharma and artha, nor are they adequate in valour against the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: na hīme sarvarājānaḥ paryāptāḥ sahitās tvayā kruddhasya bhīmasenasya prekṣituṃ mukham āhave
english: "Indeed, all these kings together with you are not capable of facing the wrathful Bhīmasena in battle."

sanskrit: idaṃ saṃnihitaṃ tāta samagraṃ pārthivaṃ balam ayaṃ bhīṣmas tathā droṇaḥ karṇaś cāyaṃ tathā kṛpaḥ
english: "All this assembled royal army that stands here, dear boy — Bhīṣma, and Droṇa, and Karṇa, and Kṛpa —"

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ saumadattir aśvatthāmā jayadrathaḥ aśaktāḥ sarva evaite pratiyoddhuṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: "Bhūriśravas, Saumadatti, Aśvatthāmā, and Jayadratha — all of these are incapable of standing against Dhanañjaya in battle."

sanskrit: ajeyo hy arjunaḥ kruddhaḥ sarvair api surāsuraiḥ mānuṣair api gandharvair mā yuddhe ceta ādhithāḥ
english: "Arjuna when enraged is unconquerable by all gods and demons, by humans and by Gandharvas alike — do not set your heart on war."

sanskrit: dṛśyatāṃ vā pumān kaś cit samagre pārthive bale yo 'rjunaṃ samare prāpya svastimān āvrajed gṛhān
english: "Let us see if there is any man in all this assembled royal army who, having encountered Arjuna in battle, would return home unharmed."

sanskrit: kiṃ te janakṣayeṇeha kṛtena bharatarṣabha yasmiñ jite jitaṃ te syāt pumān ekaḥ sa dṛśyatām
english: "What good to you is the slaughter of people here, O bull among Bhāratas? Let that one man be pointed out by whose defeat you would be victorious."

sanskrit: yaḥ sa devān sagandharvān sayakṣāsurapannagān ajayat khāṇḍavaprasthe kas taṃ yudhyeta mānavaḥ
english: "He who at Khāṇḍavaprastha conquered the gods, the Gandharvas, the Yakṣas, the Asuras, and the Nāgas together — what mortal would fight him?"

sanskrit: tathā virāṭanagare śrūyate mahad adbhutam ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: "Likewise at the city of Virāṭa a great wonder is heard — of one against many; that example is sufficient proof."

sanskrit: tam ajeyam anādhṛṣyaṃ vijetuṃ jiṣṇum acyutam āśaṃsasīha samare vīram arjunam ūrjitam
english: "Yet you hope to conquer in battle that unconquerable, unapproachable, victorious, unwavering, mighty hero Arjuna."

sanskrit: maddvitīyaṃ punaḥ pārthaṃ kaḥ prārthayitum arhati yuddhe pratīpam āyāntam api sākṣāt puraṃdaraḥ
english: "Who would dare challenge Pārtha when I am his companion, advancing in battle against them? Not even Indra himself could do so."

sanskrit: bāhubhyām uddhared bhūmiṃ dahet kruddha imāḥ prajāḥ pātayet tridivād devān yo 'rjunaṃ samare jayet
english: "He who defeats Arjuna in battle would have to lift the earth with his bare arms, burn these people in his wrath, and hurl the gods from heaven."

sanskrit: paśya putrāṃs tathā bhrātṝñ jñātīn saṃbandhinas tathā tvatkṛte na vinaśyeyur ete bharatasattama
english: "Consider your sons, your brothers, your kinsmen and relatives — let them not perish on your account, O best of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: astu śeṣaṃ kauravāṇāṃ mā parābhūd idaṃ kulam kulaghna iti nocyethā naṣṭakīrtir narādhipa
english: "Let there remain a remnant of the Kauravas; let this lineage not be destroyed; let it not be said of you 'destroyer of the family,' your fame ruined, O lord of men."

sanskrit: tvām eva sthāpayiṣyanti yauvarājye mahārathāḥ mahārājye ca pitaraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram
english: "The great warriors will establish you in the position of crown prince and your father Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, as sovereign king."

sanskrit: mā tāta śriyam āyāntīm avamaṃsthāḥ samudyatām ardhaṃ pradāya pārthebhyo mahatīṃ śriyam āpsyasi
english: "Do not disregard the prosperity that is coming toward you, already poised; by giving half to the Pārthas you will obtain great prosperity."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavaiḥ saṃśamaṃ kṛtvā kṛtvā ca suhṛdāṃ vacaḥ saṃprīyamāṇo mitraiś ca ciraṃ bhadrāṇy avāpsyasi
english: "Having made peace with the Pāṇḍavas, having heeded the counsel of your friends, and delighting in your allies, you will long enjoy good fortune."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo duryodhanam amarṣaṇam keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā provāca bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, having heard the words of Keśava, spoke to the impatient Duryodhana, O bull among Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇena vākyam ukto 'si suhṛdāṃ śamam icchatā anupaśyasva tat tāta mā manyuvaśam anvagāḥ
english: "You have been addressed in words by Kṛṣṇa, who desires the welfare of his friends; reflect on that, dear boy; do not follow the lead of anger."

sanskrit: akṛtvā vacanaṃ tāta keśavasya mahātmanaḥ śreyo na jātu na sukhaṃ na kalyāṇam avāpsyasi
english: "Without acting on the word of the great-souled Keśava, dear boy, you will never obtain the highest good, nor happiness, nor well-being."

sanskrit: dharmyam arthaṃ mahābāhur āha tvāṃ tāta keśavaḥ tam artham abhipadyasva mā rājan nīnaśaḥ prajāḥ
english: "The mighty-armed Keśava has spoken to you a righteous and beneficial purpose, dear boy; adopt that purpose, O king; do not destroy your people."

sanskrit: imāṃ śriyaṃ prajvalitāṃ bhāratīṃ sarvarājasu jīvato dhṛtarāṣṭrasya daurātmyād bhraṃśayiṣyasi
english: "Through your wickedness you will cause to fall this blazing Bhārata sovereignty renowned among all kings, while Dhṛtarāṣṭra yet lives."

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ ca sahāmātyaṃ saputrapaśubāndhavam sahamitram asadbuddhyā jīvitād bhraṃśayiṣyasi
english: "Through your evil counsel you will cause to fall from life yourself together with your ministers, sons, cattle, kinsmen, and allies."

sanskrit: atikrāman keśavasya tathyaṃ vacanam arthavat pituś ca bharataśreṣṭha vidurasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: "By transgressing the true and purposeful counsel of Keśava, and that of your father, O best of Bhāratas, and of the wise Vidura —"

sanskrit: mā kulaghno 'ntapuruṣo durmatiḥ kāpathaṃ gamaḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ caiva vṛddhau śokāya mā dadaḥ
english: "— do not go the wrong path as a destroyer of your family, a last man, a wretch; do not give your aged father and mother over to grief."

sanskrit: atha droṇo 'bravīt tatra duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ amarṣavaśam āpannaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then Droṇa spoke there these words to Duryodhana, who had fallen under the sway of wrath and was sighing again and again.

sanskrit: dharmārthayuktaṃ vacanam āha tvāṃ tāta keśavaḥ tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas taj juṣasva narādhipa
english: "Keśava has spoken to you a word joined with dharma and worldly good, dear boy, and Bhīṣma son of Śaṃtanu likewise; accept it, O lord of men."

sanskrit: prājñau medhāvinau dāntāv arthakāmau bahuśrutau āhatus tvāṃ hitaṃ vākyaṃ tad ādatsva paraṃtapa
english: "Two wise men, intelligent, self-controlled, caring for your welfare, and learned, have spoken to you a beneficial word; accept it, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: anutiṣṭha mahāprājña kṛṣṇabhīṣmau yad ūcatuḥ mā vaco laghubuddhīnāṃ samāsthās tvaṃ paraṃtapa
english: "Follow what Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma have said, O greatly wise one; do not follow the words of the shallow-minded, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: ye tvāṃ protsāhayanty ete naite kṛtyāya karhi cit vairaṃ pareṣāṃ grīvāyāṃ pratimokṣyanti saṃyuge
english: "Those who are inciting you — they are never of any use to you; in battle they will fasten the enemy's enmity around their own necks."

sanskrit: mā kurūñ jīghanaḥ sarvān putrān bhrātṝṃs tathaiva ca vāsudevārjunau yatra viddhy ajeyaṃ balaṃ hi tat
english: "Do not slay all the Kurus — their sons and brothers alike; where Vāsudeva and Arjuna stand, know that their force is unconquerable."

sanskrit: etac caiva mataṃ satyaṃ suhṛdoḥ kṛṣṇabhīṣmayoḥ yadi nādāsyase tāta paścāt tapsyasi bhārata
english: "This indeed is the true view of your two well-wishers, Kṛṣṇa and Bhīṣma; if you do not accept it, dear boy, you will repent hereafter, O Bhārata."
